summary: The milestone is honestly scoped, the staging decisions (q4km-coopmat fusion deferred, cuBLAS-as-estimate, NVIDIA-first) are defensible, Lever A is correctly re-landed without ReBAR, and the 4096x4096 footprint is ~400MB worst-case (far under the 50GB cap). HN-1 (VulkanMemoryModel device feature) is REAL and correctly identified by reading the codegen: emit.rs lines 148-159 emit OpMemoryModel Logical Vulkan + OpCapability VulkanMemoryModel whenever coopmat is used, and context.rs currently chains NEITHER. HOWEVER the design has THREE blocking gaps that the architect did not surface, all verified against actual code: (C1) the runtime has NO way to know a kernel is coopmat or what shape it requires — KernelMetadata (metadata.rs:45) carries no coopmat descriptor, CoopMatKey (axc-hir/coopmat.rs:206) has NO K dimension and NO distinct result_type, and @cooperative_matrix is a bare bool flag (hir.rs:101) with no M/N/K/types — so HN-10's 'build CoopMatRequiredShape from the kernel metadata, not a literal' and AT-1551's 'nothing hardcoded' are NOT achievable without a KernelMetadata schema bump that the design omits; (C2) matmul_tile reads/writes f16 SSBOs (StorageBuffer16BitAccess capability is emitted) and is the FIRST-EVER kernel to be dispatched that needs 16-bit storage — but the device feature storageBuffer16BitAccess (Vulkan11Features / 16BitStorageFeatures) is NOT enabled anywhere and the design only chains CooperativeMatrix+VulkanMemoryModel, so pipeline creation will fail on a conformant NVIDIA driver for a reason ORTHOGONAL to HN-1; (C3) the same omission applies to the q4km path (StorageBuffer8BitAccess + Int8 + Int16 device features) — confirmed there is currently NO GPU-dispatch test for ANY 8-bit/16-bit kernel (only saxpy/vector_add f32 dispatch today), so this whole feature-enablement surface is untested and under-specified. Fix C1/C2/C3 and the milestone is sound.
critical_issues: CRITICAL-1 (shape metadata does not exist — breaks HN-10 and AT-1551): The runtime cannot construct CoopMatRequiredShape{m,n,k,a/b/c/result} from kernel metadata because that metadata is absent. Verified: KernelMetadata (crates/axc-runtime/src/metadata.rs:45-68) has schema_version/kernel_name/workgroup_size/binding_plan/push_constant_total_bytes/entry_point and NOTHING coopmat. CoopMatKey (crates/axc-hir/src/coopmat.rs:206-211) is {elem, m, n, use_} — NO k, NO result_type. @cooperative_matrix lowers to a bare `cooperative_matrix: bool` (crates/axc-hir/src/hir.rs:101; lower.rs:126) with NO M/N/K/type arguments. Therefore: (a) the runtime cannot even DETECT that matmul_tile is a coopmat kernel to apply the CoopMatUnsupported gate (AT-1505), and (b) the required 16x16x16-f16-Subgroup shape can ONLY be hardcoded in the test — directly contradicting HN-10 ('not a literal') and AT-1551 ('nothing hardcoded'). REQUIRED: either (i) extend KernelMetadata with a coopmat descriptor {is_coopmat, m, n, k, a_type, b_type, c_type, result_type, scope} and BUMP CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION (cost not accounted in the plan, and CoopMatKey/typecheck must surface K + result_type which they currently do not for the accumulator), OR (ii) HONESTLY restate the design to admit the M3.1 required shape is a test-side constant and drop the 'nothing hardcoded' claims from HN-10/AT-1551. The current text claims (i) but specifies (ii).

CRITICAL-2 (16-bit storage DEVICE FEATURE not enabled — second pipeline-create footgun, distinct from HN-1): matmul_tile.axc binds readonly_buffer[f16] x2 + buffer[f16]; emit.rs (lines 137-139, 336-338) emits OpCapability StorageBuffer16BitAccess + OpExtension SPV_KHR_16bit_storage for f16 SSBOs. A conformant driver REQUIRES VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Features.storageBuffer16BitAccess (or VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures.storageBuffer16BitAccess) enabled at device creation or vkCreateComputePipelines fails with the SHADER module rejected — EXACTLY the 'spirv-val passes, pipeline-create fails' class the architect warns about in HN-1, but the design's vulkan_features_extensions ONLY chains CooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR + VulkanMemoryModelFeatures + (unchanged) Vulkan12Features. storageBuffer16BitAccess is NEVER chained. Verified context.rs (lines 344-356) enables only vk12_features.timeline_semaphore. This is the FIRST f16-SSBO kernel ever dispatched (today only saxpy/vector_add f32 dispatch). REQUIRED: chain the 16-bit storage feature (and, if any f16 arithmetic ends up in coopmat-adjacent code, shaderFloat16) whenever a kernel needs 16-bit storage; the decision must be driven by binding-plan inspection, not coopmat-presence, because plain f16 SSBO kernels need it too.

CRITICAL-3 (8-bit storage + Int8/Int16 device features not enabled for the q4km matmul path): examples/q4km_dequant_matmul.axc binds readonly_buffer[u8]; emit.rs (lines 141-143, 345-355) emits StorageBuffer8BitAccess + Int8 (+ Int16 for f16_bits_to_f32). These require VkPhysicalDevice{8BitStorage,ShaderFloat16Int8}Features.storageBuffer8BitAccess / shaderInt8 (and Vulkan11/12 shaderInt16) enabled at device creation. None are chained today, and the plan does not add them. Confirmed there is NO existing GPU-dispatch test for any 8-bit/16-bit kernel (tests/ has only compile_q4km_*, compile_q4_0_*; the only dispatched kernels are saxpy/vector_add). AT-1520 asserts q4km_dequant_matmul DISPATCHES on Lavapipe AND NVIDIA within 1e-3 — on conformant NVIDIA this will fail at pipeline create unless these features are enabled. REQUIRED: a binding-plan-driven feature-enablement pass that turns each emitted storage/int capability into its device-feature toggle, with graceful fallback (skip, not crash) when a target lacks the feature.

CRITICAL-4 (no test proves a TRANSPOSED / mis-strided coopmat_load is caught — the classic silent-miscompute hole): The oracle is f16-ULP+abs tolerance on a 16x16 C=A*B with C0=0. matmul_tile uses RowMajorKHR for BOTH A and B (codegen ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, coopmat.rs:79) and the SAME tile_offset+stride for a_buf, b_buf, c_buf. A transposed B-load, a swapped A/B, or a stride bug produces a WRONG result that a loose f16 tol on a symmetric/uniform fixture can mask. The design's fixtures are 'small values in [-1,1]' seeded but the plan does NOT mandate a NON-SYMMETRIC, NON-square-friendly fixture (e.g. A != A^T, B != B^T, distinct row/col magnitude gradients, an asymmetric C0 offset) whose correct product differs maximally from its transpose. REQUIRED: AT-1510 must use a fixture where A*B, A^T*B, A*B^T, and B*A are all numerically distinct beyond the tolerance, so a transpose/stride/operand-swap bug cannot pass.
warnings: WARNING (HN-1 lifetime/p_next chaining): the design says chain CooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR + VulkanMemoryModelFeatures 'alongside the existing Vulkan12Features push_next'. context.rs only constructs vk12_features in the timeline+1.2 branch (lines 346-356); on a 1.1 device or non-timeline path that local is never pushed. Coder must ensure the coopmat + memory-model + storage features are chained UNCONDITIONALLY when needed, with ALL feature-struct locals outliving create_device — a borrow/lifetime trap that the current single-branch code structure invites getting wrong. Specify the exact p_next chain assembly for the non-1.2 case.

WARNING (preflight: extension advertised, ZERO properties): handled in edge_cases ('zero shapes despite feature_present true -> skip') — good. But also guard the two-call idiom: if the count returned by the first vkGetPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR is 0, do NOT call the second with a non-null pointer expecting >0; return empty shapes. Make the AT-1501 test cover count==0-with-ext-present, not only ext-absent.

WARNING (matcher must reject near-misses including scope, result_type, AND saturatingAccumulation): VkCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR reports scope, MSize/NSize/KSize, AType/BType/CType/ResultType, AND saturatingAccumulation. The plan's matcher (technical_spec) compares m/n/k + component types + scope==Subgroup but does NOT mention ResultType vs CType distinction for the f16 accumulator (NVIDIA commonly reports f16 A/B with f16 OR f32 C/Result variants) nor saturatingAccumulation (must be VK_FALSE for the f16 GEMM since codegen passes NONE_KHR operands, coopmat.rs:189). AT-1561 covers the f16-c-vs-f32-c discrimination — good — but the plan never states the kernel's REQUIRED result_type, and CoopMatKey has no result_type field to source it from (see CRITICAL-1). A near-miss on result_type would silently miscompute.

WARNING (graceful-skip can GREEN a test that never ran — anti-pattern #9 surface): On Lavapipe every coopmat AT skips; if the NVIDIA runner is not MANDATORY in the dev-box test run, AT-1510 (the load-bearing first-dispatch proof) can be perpetually skipped while CI shows green. The design must state that the NVIDIA runner is a REQUIRED gate for M3.1 sign-off (not optional), and that a skip on ALL available devices is a milestone FAIL, not a pass. AT-1506 force_no_coopmat exercises the skip path on NVIDIA but does NOT substitute for proving the dispatch path.

WARNING (timestamp masking + reset ordering): HN-6 is correct (mask to timestamp_valid_bits, fall back to wall). Two specifics to pin: (a) mask BEFORE subtracting (mask each of begin/end to valid_bits, then subtract with wrapping) so a wrap across the valid-bit boundary doesn't yield a garbage huge delta; (b) cmd_reset_query_pool MUST be recorded before the first write_timestamp in the SAME submission (or pool reset host-side) or results are undefined on re-dispatch in the resident N-loop. Also vkCmdWriteTimestamp at TOP_OF_PIPE measures from when the GPU REACHES that command, not steady-state; for 'kernel-only' honesty document that queue/scheduling latency before TOP is excluded by design.

WARNING (resident bench leaks / descriptor aliasing across N dispatches): HN-8 documents not interleaving dispatch_handle and dispatch_resident, and ResidentBuffers owns a separate lifetime — good. But the N-iteration loop must REUSE one command buffer (reset+rerecord or pre-record once) and one fence; allocating a CB or query pool per iteration across, e.g., thousands of iterations could exhaust the pool. Specify single-allocation reuse for the steady-state loop. Footprint itself is fine: 4096^2 f32 = 64MB/matrix, ~400MB incl. device+staging for 3 matrices — well under 50GB.

WARNING (subgroup-size assumption is documented but the .axc is silently NVIDIA-tuned): @workgroup(32,1,1) == one subgroup only on a 32-lane vendor. On AMD wave64 the workgroup would span 2 subgroups and the single-tile mapping is WRONG, not just unsupported — but the preflight only checks shape support, not subgroup-size/workgroup-to-subgroup consistency. The design defers AMD/Intel (acceptable for NVIDIA-first) BUT must ensure a wave64 device that DOES advertise 16x16x16 f16 Subgroup support is still SKIPPED (or the test is NVIDIA-pinned), otherwise it could dispatch and silently miscompute. Add an explicit subgroupSize==32 guard (or device-vendor pin) to the matmul_tile dispatch, not just a shape check.
principle_violations: VIOLATION (anti-pattern: 'no silent extension/feature picking' + explicitness): enabling VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix and the storage/int device features 'when advertised' is implicit feature acquisition. The capabilities are explicit in the EMITTED SPIR-V (good), but the device-feature enablement must be a deterministic function of the binding plan + caps, documented per-kernel, not a best-effort 'enable what the device has'. Make the feature set REQUIRED-BY-MODULE (derive from emitted capabilities) and FAIL-CLOSED with a typed skip when the device lacks a required feature — never enable-and-hope.

VIOLATION (HN-10 vs AT-1551 internal contradiction): the design simultaneously claims the required shape is read from metadata (HN-10) and that 'nothing is hardcoded' (AT-1551) while the type/metadata plumbing to do so does not exist (CRITICAL-1). One of these claims is false as written; the milestone must not ship a self-contradictory honesty claim.
spirv_concerns: Confirmed by reading codegen: emit.rs emits OpCapability CooperativeMatrixKHR (via caps.coopmat path, lines 318-325), VulkanMemoryModel (148-159), Float16 (330-331), StorageBuffer16BitAccess (336-338), and for q4km Int8/StorageBuffer8BitAccess/Int16 (345-355), plus the matching OpExtensions. spirv_capabilities_required in the plan matches what is emitted. spirv-val (AT-1511/AT-1560) validates the MODULE — but spirv-val does NOT check device-feature enablement; passing spirv-val does NOT imply the pipeline will create. The plan correctly separates these in HN-1 but UNDER-COUNTS the device features needed (only memory-model+coopmat; misses 16-bit/8-bit storage + Int8/Int16). See CRITICAL-2/-3.

OpCooperativeMatrixMulAddKHR uses NONE_KHR operands (coopmat.rs:189) => non-saturating; the preflight matcher must therefore require saturatingAccumulation==VK_FALSE on the matched property or reject — not in the current matcher spec (see warnings).
vendor_concerns: NVIDIA Blackwell (RTX PRO 6000): subgroup size 32, advertises 16x16x16 f16 Subgroup — the target. Must enable storageBuffer16BitAccess + VulkanMemoryModel + cooperativeMatrix features or pipeline-create fails (CRITICAL-2, HN-1).

Lavapipe (Mesa lvp): no VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix -> skip path (correct). But Lavapipe is also LAX about 16-bit/8-bit storage feature enforcement, which means the q4km/f16 pipeline-create may SUCCEED on Lavapipe while FAILING on NVIDIA — masking CRITICAL-2/-3 in CI and surfacing only on the dev-box NVIDIA run. Do not let Lavapipe success imply NVIDIA success.

AMD wave64 / Intel SIMD16: @workgroup(32,1,1) is unsafe if such a device advertises the shape; needs subgroupSize==32 guard or NVIDIA pin (see warnings). Deferral of AMD/Intel dispatch to EB.1/M3.4 is acceptable IF the skip is guaranteed, not merely shape-gated.
missing_tests: MUST TEST: a NON-SYMMETRIC, transpose-distinguishing 16x16 fixture for AT-1510 so a transposed/swapped/mis-strided coopmat_load cannot pass the f16 tolerance (CRITICAL-4).

MUST TEST: pipeline CREATION succeeds for matmul_tile on a device with coopmat+16-bit-storage features enabled, as a step BEFORE dispatch (HN-1 says 'test pipeline creation before dispatch' — encode it as an explicit AT, e.g. AT-1509, distinct from spirv-val and from the dispatch correctness AT).

MUST TEST: pipeline creation for q4km_dequant_matmul (8-bit storage + Int8/Int16) on NVIDIA — currently NO 8/16-bit kernel has ever been dispatch-tested; AT-1520 implicitly requires it but the feature enablement is unspecified.
MUST TEST: preflight matcher rejects a property whose ResultType differs from the required accumulator type and whose saturatingAccumulation==VK_TRUE (extend AT-1561).
MUST TEST: timestamp valid-bits masking with a synthetic begin/end straddling the valid-bit boundary returns a sane delta (unit-testable without GPU).
MUST CONFIRM: the NVIDIA runner is a MANDATORY gate; a run where AT-1510 skips on every available device is a FAIL (anti-pattern #9).
questions_for_architect: Q1 (blocking): How does the runtime DETECT that a compiled kernel is a coopmat kernel and learn its required (M,N,K,a/b/c/result,scope) shape, given KernelMetadata carries none of this and CoopMatKey lacks K and result_type? If via a KernelMetadata schema bump, specify the new fields, the CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION bump, and the typecheck/emit plumbing that fills them. If the test hardcodes the shape, retract HN-10/AT-1551's 'nothing hardcoded'.

Q2 (blocking): Where are storageBuffer16BitAccess (f16 SSBO), storageBuffer8BitAccess + shaderInt8 + shaderInt16 (q4km) device features enabled? They are emitted as SPIR-V capabilities but never chained at device creation today. Specify a binding-plan/caps-driven feature-enablement pass with fail-closed typed skip.
Q3: Does the matcher compare ResultType and saturatingAccumulation, not just M/N/K + A/B/C component types + scope? What is the kernel's REQUIRED result_type and where is it sourced?
Q4: Is the NVIDIA runner a mandatory M3.1 gate, and is an all-device-skip of AT-1510 treated as FAIL?
Q5: For wave64/SIMD16 devices that advertise 16x16x16 f16 Subgroup support, is there a subgroupSize==32 guard preventing a silent miscompute, or is matmul_tile dispatch NVIDIA-pinned?

open_question_positions.OQ-1 (NVIDIA-first 32-lane assumption): ACCEPTABLE for M3.1 ONLY IF a subgroupSize==32 (or vendor-pin) guard prevents dispatch on a wave64 device that happens to advertise the shape (see CRITICAL warnings). Defer the @strategy workgroup-size hole to M3.4. Do not ship shape-only gating.
open_question_positions.OQ-2 (Lavapipe skip mechanics): AGREE with the proposal: tests inspect ctx.coopmat_support() to decide skip, AND AT-1505 also asserts the typed CoopMatUnsupported error if dispatch is attempted. BUT this is moot until Q1 is resolved — the runtime cannot evaluate coopmat_shape_supported without knowing the kernel's required shape.
open_question_positions.OQ-3 (q4km-coopmat fusion staging): AGREE the staged split is honest and sufficient; do NOT attempt the shared[T,N] fusion now (correctly deferred to M3.2). The plain multi-row q4km matmul as the bit-exact deliverable + a pre-dequantized coopmat bridge is the right honesty boundary. No bloat.
open_question_positions.OQ-4 (resident API surface): Method form with documented HN-8 caveat is ACCEPTABLE for a single-threaded bench; a type-enforced ResidentSession is nicer but not worth the surface for M3.1. Require single-allocation CB/fence/query-pool reuse in the N-loop regardless of which form.
open_question_positions.OQ-5 (cuBLAS estimate constant): ASSERT only effective TFLOPS (2MNK/sec) as AT-1532; keep the >=50%-of-cuBLAS as informational, clearly labeled an external estimate with a sourced constant. This is the honest floor. Do NOT make the ratio a hard gate. Agree with the proposal.
open_question_positions.OQ-6 (DispatchError count test rename): AGREE: keep at_801 name, bump asserted count 28->29, add CoopMatUnsupported to the exhaustive vec (verified current count is 28 in error.rs:7,251-306). Mirrors the AT-502 alias precedent. Trivial; non-blocking.

most_dangerous_hole: The single most dangerous hole is CRITICAL-1 compounded by CRITICAL-4: the runtime has no metadata to know matmul_tile is a coopmat kernel or what shape it requires (so the required 16x16x16 f16 shape must be hardcoded in the test, falsifying HN-10/AT-1551), AND the only correctness oracle is a loose f16 tolerance on a transpose-friendly fixture with RowMajor loads sharing one stride/offset for A and B. Together these mean a transposed/swapped/mis-strided coopmat_load could pass AT-1510 while the system simultaneously claims 'nothing hardcoded' — a correctness miscompute hidden behind an honesty claim that the codebase cannot actually support. CRITICAL-2 (unenabled 16-bit-storage device feature) is the most likely to FAIL LOUDLY first (pipeline-create error on NVIDIA), which is the lucky case; the metadata+transpose hole is the one that fails SILENTLY.
summary_final: NEEDS_REVISION. The scope honesty, staging, Lever A re-land, footprint, and the HN-1 VulkanMemoryModel insight are all sound and verified. Block coding until: (C1) coopmat shape detection/metadata is specified (schema bump or honest hardcode admission, resolving the HN-10/AT-1551 contradiction); (C2/C3) 16-bit and 8-bit storage + Int8/Int16 DEVICE features are enabled via a binding-plan/caps-driven pass with fail-closed skip (these are the FIRST 8/16-bit dispatch ever; only memory-model+coopmat are currently planned); (C4) AT-1510 uses a transpose-distinguishing non-symmetric fixture. Add a pre-dispatch pipeline-creation AT, a result_type+saturatingAccumulation matcher check, a subgroupSize==32 guard, and make the NVIDIA runner a mandatory gate so anti-pattern #9 cannot be skip-gamed.
